video.title: Shoulder Adduction Will Transform Your Forehand Contact

classification.reason: The coach provides executable drills and instructions, such as matching grip to comfortable shoulder adduction without holding a racket first, and focusing solely on shoulder adduction during mini tennis.

problem.title_as_question: How does shoulder adduction determine forehand contact and consistency?
problem.definition: Forehand contact and hitting zone stability are fundamentally created by horizontal shoulder adduction and internal rotation. Without understanding and establishing this feeling, upstream body rotation, swing speed, and topspin only lead to more misses.

symptoms.description: Erratic contact and missing more when trying to swing faster or add topspin without solid shoulder adduction mechanics.
Throwing the racket finish above the head (buggy whip style) when the ball is too close to the body in an attempt to preserve the adduction feeling.

causes.statement: The player does not close the pectoral-humeral angle via horizontal shoulder adduction and internal rotation through contact to press the arm forward.
The player's grip does not match what is anatomically natural and comfortable for their specific horizontal shoulder adduction stroke, corrupting string angle.
The player focuses on upstream kinetic chain elements like torso rotation, stance drive, and swing speed while the foundational contact mechanics are broken.
On low balls, the player fails to tilt the torso and bend the back knee, preventing the chest and shoulder from performing horizontal adduction on plane.

angles.summary: Forehand velocity through contact is created by the pectoral muscles pressing the hand forward as the pectoral-humeral angle closes.
Body and torso rotation are not mandatory to hit a decent forehand; shoulder adduction is the non-negotiable requirement at contact.
When a ball is too close to the body, players naturally reverse or whip the racket above the head to preserve the feeling of chest pressing and shoulder adduction.

solutions.summary: Perform a shadow adduction swing without a racket to find your body's natural motion, then place the racket into the hand at contact to find the grip that yields a slightly closed string angle.
solutions.external_goal: A slightly closed string angle at the contact point.

solutions.summary: Practice hitting shots while keeping the chest stationary and only adducting the shoulder across the body to isolate contact mechanics without torso rotation.
When dealing with a low ball, tilt the torso, drop the back knee into an athletic stance, and push the arm forward across the chest so adduction can happen naturally on plane.
During mini tennis, focus purely on feeling horizontal shoulder adduction and finding the contact spot in front where it happens naturally.
solutions.external_goal: Find that spot in front of you where adduction happens naturally.

solutions.summary: Check that you prepare away from the body, adduct the shoulder cleanly through the ball, and keep eyes on contact the entire time.
